projectDesc.p: One colophon per TEI file, with a witness division where required, a general mise-en-page description, folio divisions containing Armenian and English text blocks, inline passage notes, and one final commentary section. Authority records identify the colophon, witness, manuscript, entities, events, lemmata, and publications.

editorialDecl.p: Keep the source transcription separate from the translation and editorial commentary. Adopted policies for punctuation, abbreviation expansion, and normalisation are recorded in editorial standard doc which will be published alongside final populated edition. Editorial intervention must remain visible.
For each folio division, use ab type="transcription" xml:lang="xcl" and ab type="translation" xml:lang="en". Translation corresp points to the Armenian block.

Each folio division identifies the page and links to its facsimile. Record column changes with cb and line beginnings with lb. English cb/lb retain the supplied editorial alignment. Keep n only every five lines, restarting in each column; no routine line IDs.

Describe mise en page for this witness and relevant folios: placement, relationship to surrounding text, columns, spacing, indentation, headings, rubrication, decoration, and relevant script or hand contrasts. A later copy may have different layout from the colophon's original inscription.
Encode passage-specific commentary inline using an anchor type="commentary" with a short xml:id before the explained passage, followed by note type="commentary" with corresp pointing to that anchor.
Armenian formula seg/@ana links directly to standard-pattern definitions in formulae.xml. Formula classifications follow authority/formulae.xml.

Words in the Armenian transcription use lemma, the exact GREgORI pos code, lemmaRef for the lexical record, and contextual msd values documented in ../authority/pos.xml. Nominal order is case.number, such as Nom.Pl; finite verbal order is tense-or-stem.mood.voice.person.number, such as Aor.Ind.Pass.3.Sg. Non-finite order is form.voice.case.number, such as Part.Dat.Sg. Record only applicable, established features, retaining their order. Pres.Sub and Aor.Sub distinguish stem formations, not temporal meaning. Tag each component of a compound verbal construction according to its own form. Non-finite forms receive no grammatical person. Explain unresolved analysis separately rather than treating it as inapplicable.
Use persName/@ref, placeName/@ref, and title/@ref for identified entities in English. Collective designations use rs/@type="people" with a personGrp reference.

Document production/post-production classification separately from witness transmission status and date. A copied production colophon remains a production colophon even though its surviving inscription is later. Dates narrated by the text do not automatically date the physical witness.

revisionDesc.change: Created the first working case edition for single colophon witness from Yerevan, Mesrop Mashtots Institute of Ancient Manuscripts, MS. 288 transcription and translations.

div.head: Colophon 1 — Yerevan, Mesrop Mashtots Institute of Ancient Manuscripts, MS. 288, fols. 278v–280v 1099 CE (Armenian era 548), Alexandria

div.ab: The supplied transcription locates the colophon in column B of 278v, columns A and B of 279r, 279v, and 280r, and column A of 280v. It records 11 lines on 278v B; 19 and 20 on 279r A/B; 19 and 19 on 279v A/B; 19 and 18 on 280r A/B; and 10 on 280v A. Placement relative to Gospel text, spacing, rubrication, decoration, and hands have not yet been described.

div.head: Folio 278v
div.ab:
Glory to the Three,
to the Infinite,
to the Able and UnableIn an apophatic theological sense. Apophatic theology can be found as prominent fixture in the near contemporary tenth-century Armenian theological works of Grigory of Narek. Prayers 23 and 92 of his Book of Lamentations, by way of example, carry some verbal parallels to the doxological language in this colophon: Narek (2008) 167, 552 .,
to the Tripersonal unity, to those who are OriginalIn the sense of originally existent: Իսկութիւն..
In the Armenian year
548 (1099), this Holy Gospel
was written,
by the hand of Aharovn,
an ignorant and contemptible
scribe, and an unworthy
monk.

Now, I pray

div.head: Folio 279v

ab.note: բացին (lemma բանալ, “to open”) is used here in the sense of “conquer”: a semantic Arabicism comparable to Arabic فتح.

div.ab:
Now, this holy Gospel
was written
during the
patriarchate
of Lord Gregory,
under the sovereignty
of the Romans,
of the Aryan Արեաց: literally “valiant ones”. This term is often used in classical Armenian literature in connection with the Iranian world, signalling those who were conceptually part of Eranšahr, as allies of Ohrmazd in the struggle against Ahreman: Greenwood (2019). Here it is used to refer to the Frankish crusaders, as we find in other contemporary colophons.
people who
are the Franks,
who had come
in their
multitude
through the
instigation of
the almighty God. And they came
as far as
Antioch and
with great toil
and warfare,
they captured
the city
and with sharp swords
they mercilessly
slaughtered the
impious. And
after three days
an innumerable
host
of Turks թուրքաց ,
Persians պարսից , Arabs արապկաց
and Muslims տաճկաց ,
arrived and encircled
the city
and the plain,
numbering four
hundred thousand and
forty thousand.

With
heavenly
assistance

In the same yearHere referring to the Armenian era 548 (1099 CE), which is stated earlier in the colophon., they captured
